title: TRAIN-2 with Phesgo

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: Cells use tiny structures called microtubules to separate their chromosomes when dividing. Paclitaxel stabilises these structures so they cannot rearrange normally, interrupting cell division. It can also affect nerves and other healthy tissues.
agents.watch: Report tingling or numbness before the next next dose, especially if it affects walking or hand use. Tell the nurse immediately about flushing, chest or throat tightness, itching, dizziness or breathing changes during infusion.
risks: Hair loss, muscle or joint pain
Mouth, bowel, skin and nail effects

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin creates links in DNA, making it harder for cells to copy and repair their genetic instructions. Its dose depends on kidney function as well as the intended regimen.
agents.watch: Keep blood-test appointments. Fever, unusual bleeding, repeated vomiting or infusion symptoms need prompt advice.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Allergic reaction, sometimes after previous exposure

agents.name: Pertuzumab
agents.alias: Part of the combined Phesgo injection
agents.mechanism: Blocks HER2 pairing with other receptors
agents.explanation: Pertuzumab binds a different area of HER2 from trastuzumab. It limits receptor pairing, so the two antibodies act together at different points on the same growth pathway.
agents.watch: Keep echo appointments. Report diarrhoea, new breathlessness, swelling, palpitations or an injection reaction.

agents.name: Trastuzumab
agents.alias: Part of the combined Phesgo injection
agents.explanation: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
agents.watch: Keep echo appointments. Report diarrhoea, new breathlessness, swelling, palpitations or an injection reaction.

medicines_title: Two antibodies in one injection with chemotherapy
timeline_note: Treatment days show the planned pattern. Symptom bands are broad possibilities, not measured risk curves or a prediction of when you will feel unwell.
safety_note: Serious symptoms need assessment on any day, even if the chart shows a usual recovery period.
teachback: Which medicines are active now, when is your next echo or scan due, and who will review it?
consent_support: Discuss the aim, alternatives, uncertain benefit, common and serious risks, heart function, diarrhoea, injection reaction, fertility and pregnancy precautions. Effective contraception is required during Phesgo and for 7 months after the last dose; review the full combination and breastfeeding restrictions with the team. NCCP 00790 directs postoperative adjuvant therapy, such as trastuzumab or trastuzumab emtansine as appropriate, to complete one year. Pathology and the MDT select the actual medicine; do not assume Phesgo continuation or the metastatic 00785 code.
urgent_extra: Contact oncology promptly for new breathlessness, swelling, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink or sudden illness. Tell staff immediately about rash, chest tightness or breathing difficulty during the injection. Fever, shivers, unusual bleeding or worsening numbness during chemotherapy also need prompt advice.

support.title: Antiemetic plan
support.text: Carboplatin Day 1 uses its high-risk antiemetic plan. Day 8 paclitaxel uses a separate low-risk plan.

support.title: Premedicines
support.text: First paclitaxel dose: steroid, antihistamine and H2 blocker. Later doses: steroid is not routine unless the consultant adds it; the other premedicines follow the reviewed plan.

support.title: Appointments and results
support.text: Echo before treatment and every 12 weeks (around cycle 5 if on time), including maintenance. Bloods before each cycle. Ask who books and reviews each test; report a missing appointment.

support.title: Phase transition

questions.a: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein.

questions.q: When is my next heart scan?
questions.a: Echo or MUGA before starting and every 12 weeks during treatment, including maintenance. At an uninterrupted 21-day schedule, the first 12-week check is around cycle 5; count elapsed time from the first HER2 dose. A delay or route/phase change does not restart the clock. Cardiac concern may require 4–8-week checks or urgent earlier assessment.

NCCP 00790 directs postoperative adjuvant therapy, such as trastuzumab or trastuzumab emtansine as appropriate, to complete one year. Pathology and the MDT select the actual medicine; do not assume Phesgo continuation or the metastatic 00785 code.

Systemic neoadjuvant treatment comes before surgery. Lumpectomy versus mastectomy is agreed with the surgeon. Radiotherapy, if indicated, follows surgery/recovery and is coordinated with postoperative systemic treatment; it may overlap HER2-only treatment when both teams agree.

questions.q: Will I need CT scans, markers or DEXA?
questions.a: Baseline breast/nodal assessment and staging as indicated; assess response during neoadjuvant treatment and before surgery using the MDT-selected imaging. After local treatment, arrange mammography of remaining breast tissue; routine CT/PET or tumour markers are not asymptomatic early-breast recurrence screening. If hormone-receptor-positive disease leads to an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression, assess fracture risk and baseline DEXA when indicated. Repeat according to results, risk and the endocrine plan; DEXA is not a scan at each Phesgo cycle.

evidence.title: TRAIN-2 · three-year follow-up
evidence.intro: Evidence for the treatment strategy and for the SC formulation answer different questions.
evidence.population: HER2-positive early, locally advanced or inflammatory breast cancer at high risk of recurrence, receiving neoadjuvant treatment.
evidence.interpretation: TRAIN-2 compared anthracycline-containing and anthracycline-free strategies with IV dual HER2 blockade. The trial used nine cycles overall; the current NCCP Phesgo card specifies six cycles. Trial findings do not prove identical outcomes for this adapted schedule. FeDeriCa compared the combined subcutaneous formulation with IV pertuzumab plus trastuzumab in early breast cancer. It met the primary pharmacokinetic non-inferiority endpoint, with similar pathological response and safety findings. It was not a trial proving identical survival for every chemotherapy backbone or metastatic sequence.

chapters.title: The injection and your visit
chapters.intro: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein.

items.title: Injection and observation
items.text: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Complete the observation before chemotherapy. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin.

items.title: Switching or a treatment gap
items.text: The team checks the last dual HER2 dose, including IV treatment: a gap of less than 6 weeks uses the maintenance dose; 6 weeks or longer needs reloading. A first Phesgo visit after IV treatment does not automatically require a loading dose.

chapters.title: Scans, heart checks and bloods
chapters.intro: Agree who books, reviews and acts on each result.

items.title: Blood tests
items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle. Review required counts before Day 8 dosing under the local pre-dose pathway.

items.title: Heart ultrasound
items.text: Echo or MUGA before starting and every 12 weeks during treatment, including maintenance. At an uninterrupted 21-day schedule, the first 12-week check is around cycle 5; count elapsed time from the first HER2 dose. A delay or route/phase change does not restart the clock. Cardiac concern may require 4–8-week checks or urgent earlier assessment.

items.title: Longer-term cardiac plan
items.text: After treatment ends, agree cardiac follow-up from symptoms, risk, prior anthracyclines and the next medicine; use the active medicine’s product information and cardio-oncology plan.

items.title: Cancer imaging and markers
items.text: Baseline breast/nodal assessment and staging as indicated; assess response during neoadjuvant treatment and before surgery using the MDT-selected imaging. After local treatment, arrange mammography of remaining breast tissue; routine CT/PET or tumour markers are not asymptomatic early-breast recurrence screening.

chapters.title: Surgery, radiotherapy and hormone treatment

items.text: Systemic neoadjuvant treatment comes before surgery. Lumpectomy versus mastectomy is agreed with the surgeon. Radiotherapy, if indicated, follows surgery/recovery and is coordinated with postoperative systemic treatment; it may overlap HER2-only treatment when both teams agree.

items.title: Endocrine treatment and bone health
items.text: If hormone-receptor-positive disease leads to an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression, assess fracture risk and baseline DEXA when indicated. Repeat according to results, risk and the endocrine plan; DEXA is not a scan at each Phesgo cycle.

items.title: Receptor and genomic tests
items.text: Hormone-receptor status can affect endocrine treatment. Oncotype-type chemotherapy triage is not applied to these HER2-positive regimens; treatment selection requires the appropriate indication-specific MDT assessment.

logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan
logistics.intro: Phesgo is one combined injection of pertuzumab and trastuzumab under the skin of the thigh. It is not two separate injections and is never given into a vein.

steps.title: Before the visit
steps.text: Confirm blood results, cardiac checks, active phase, previous dual HER2 dose and the consent discussion.

steps.title: The thigh injection
steps.text: Loading/reloading 1200 mg/600 mg over 8 minutes with 30 minutes observation; maintenance 600 mg/600 mg over 5 minutes with 15 minutes observation. Complete the observation before chemotherapy. Alternate thighs; avoid sore, bruised or damaged skin.

steps.title: Chemotherapy and access
steps.text: After Phesgo observation, chemotherapy is given through a cannula, PICC or port. The team explains access insertion and care. No take-home infusion pump is routinely used.

steps.title: Leaving the unit
steps.text: Confirm supportive medicines, next visits and due tests. Injection time is shorter than the whole appointment; preparation, assessment and observation still take time.

details.title: Switching / a missed appointment
details.text: The team checks the last dual HER2 dose, including IV treatment: a gap of less than 6 weeks uses the maintenance dose; 6 weeks or longer needs reloading. A first Phesgo visit after IV treatment does not automatically require a loading dose.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.
